newsitem.title: USA: NYC settles lawsuit with H&R Block.
newsitem.headline: NYC settles lawsuit with H&R Block.

text.p: New York City's Department of Consumer Affairs has reached a settlement of its lawsuit against H&R Block Inc., in which the tax preparer will pay almost $500,000 in fines, fees and other costs, officials announced on Monday.

The lawsuit accused H&R Block of misleading consumers by blurring the distinction between its "Rapid Refund" electronically filed tax returns, and its Refund Anticipation Loans or RALs, which are high-interest loans in the amount of the anticipated return, said Consumer Affairs Commissioner Jose Maldonado.
Under terms of the settlement, H&R Block will install a phone system to prevent future deceptive trade practices, he said.
As part of the system, at a cost of almost $250,000, phone operators are under court injunction to distinguish clearly between RALs and other types of tax filings, he said.

The "Rapid Refund" products allow customers to receive tax refunds, usually in two to four weeks, Maldonado said. RALs lend taxpayers the amount of the anticipated return but charge high interest rates, he said.
"Taxpayers should not have to worry about being steered toward high interest loans by their own tax preparers," Maldonado said.
The company also will pay $200,000 in fines and $50,000 in investigation costs, he said.

The lawsuit was filed in State Supreme Court in October 1995. Investigators who posed as consumers called the tax preparation company and would reach operators who would pitch the high-interest loans, Maldonado said.
